answer: Resist sybils with an honest-edge graph bottleneck, not fees. In the dune of an interaction graph, wind erodes stale tracks, so clones must keep making real crossings. Each identity holds one non-transferable quartz anchor tied to an edge reaching honest nodes; anchors cannot be bulk-minted. A comet randomly cuts clusters whose edges never reach honest nodes. An attacker can spin up many nodes, but each survivor needs a scarce human edge plus quartz; bulk anchors are voided at the next comet. Influence follows verified crossings, not headcount.
